description: OrbitX Innovators is a team of six students passionate about technology, space science and innovation. We combine our technical skills, creativity and problem-solving abilities to develop practical solutions using NASA's open datasets. Our interests include AI, machine learning, electronics and scientific data analysis. We believe in teamwork, experimentation and innovation to solve real-world challenges.

ASTRAWELL is a Streamlit-based astronaut health monitoring and decision-support prototype designed to demonstrate how health telemetry can be collected, analysed, and presented for space missions. It monitors five key indicators: heart rate, blood oxygen saturation (SpO₂), body temperature, sleep duration, and fatigue. The system supports synthetic live telemetry, CSV-based historical baseline and new-reading analysis, anomaly detection, explainable alerts, and timestamp-based data replay. Its Mission Control dashboard provides crew monitoring, individual astronaut views, real-time telemetry charts, alert management, and advanced analytics.

ASTRAWELL aims to help identify unusual changes in astronaut health indicators by comparing readings against historical baselines and highlighting patterns for human review. The prototype uses Python, Streamlit, SQLite, and statistical analysis techniques.
details:
ASTRAWELL (Autonomous Astronaut Health Intelligence and Decision Support System) is a software prototype designed to demonstrate astronaut health monitoring and decision support during space missions. It processes health telemetry such as heart rate, blood oxygen saturation (SpO₂), body temperature, sleep duration, and fatigue.

The system provides synthetic live telemetry monitoring and CSV-based health data ingestion. It analyses historical readings to establish individual baselines, compares new readings against those baselines, identifies unusual deviations, and generates explainable alerts for human review. Its Mission Control dashboard displays astronaut monitoring cards, individual telemetry charts, crew-level analytics, and an active alert centre. It also supports timestamp-based CSV replay to demonstrate how health indicators change over time.

ASTRAWELL was developed using Python, Streamlit, SQLite, and data-analysis libraries. Its main objective is to demonstrate how health data can be organized, monitored, and analysed to help identify potentially concerning changes in astronaut health indicators.

The project's creative aspect is its integration of telemetry ingestion, baseline comparison, anomaly screening, explainable alerts, and interactive visualization into a single mission-control interface. The development considered data quality, historical comparisons, usability, data-source separation, and the limitations of automated health analysis.

The current prototype uses simulated telemetry and uploaded CSV datasets. It is not clinically validated and does not currently connect to real NASA spacecraft sensors or operational astronaut medical systems.
